title: Engine Oil Filter Housing Firewall Panel and Latch Change to Prevent Harness Chafing
abstract: Change of the oil filter housing firewall panel and its latch, after the engine harness was found chafed against the panel edge on engines that had been through more than two shop visits.

sections.reason: Three operators reported an oil quantity indication fault that resolved itself on the ground, and in each case the engine harness was found chafed where it crosses the oil filter housing firewall panel. All the affected engines had been through at least two shop visits, and the common factor was that the panel had been refitted with the latch in the alternate position permitted by the earlier drawing, which moves the panel edge four millimetres inboard onto the harness route. The failure mode is slow, produces no warning until the shield is breached, and had not been caught by the scheduled powerplant inspection.
sections.description: The firewall panel FJD382676-90 is replaced by an item with a rolled and radiused inboard edge and with the alternate latch position deleted, so that the panel can only be refitted one way. Countersunk washers AES837153-84 replace the plain washers at the six panel fasteners because the rolled edge is thicker at the flange. The seal at FIN 14EO and the cowl latch at FIN 227EO are removed and refitted, and the harness route is re-clipped one hundred millimetres further outboard. Work is in zones 431, 421 and 413 with the fan cowl open and the pylon lower access panel removed. The panel and its installation are on drawings D79201225675 and D79201232627.
sections.effects: Mass increase of 0.7 kilograms per engine. No electrical load change. One way interchangeable: the new panel fits any engine but the earlier panel must not be refitted to a modified installation because the harness has been re-routed to the new clearance. The harness chafing inspection is deleted and replaced by a general visual at each cowl opening. The oil filter housing removal task, the parts figure and the powerplant zonal inspection all require re-issue.
sections.embodiment_note: Production cut-in at MSN Z10389 in June 2021, and the engine build standard changed at the same point so that shop visits deliver modified engines. Retrofit on wing is a six hour task per engine with the fan cowl open.

type_data.production_impact: Cut-in at MSN Z10389 with the engine build standard changed together
